findings.summary: The first bullet packs two ideas: the default modifier and the fact that modifiers are compile-time only.
findings.evidence: "public, private, protected are compile-time checks only"
findings.fix: Keep it as the single idea 'compile-time only' and put 'no modifier means public' on its own bullet (already present); drop the overlap with the 'Remember' box or the erasure bullet.

findings.summary: Interface example code is shown with no one-line idea before it for the multiple-implements case, and the 'Gotchas' bullet about annotating params is unexplained.
findings.evidence: "implements does not infer params: annotate run(n: number)"
findings.fix: Add a one-line idea before the code (e.g. 'A class can extend one base and implement many interfaces') and say why: implements only checks the shape, so an unannotated parameter becomes implicit any.

findings.summary: The structural typing exception bullet bundles the rule and its consequence, and the Point example is not shown as code.
findings.evidence: "Exception: a private or protected member makes it nominal-like" / "const p: Point = { x: 1, y: 2 } works for a class Point"
findings.fix: Split into separate bullets and show a short code block contrasting a class with public members against one with a private member.

findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "believing", "security").

findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "callback", "function").

findings.summary: The 'Privacy and readonly' section states several ideas in a row as prose bullets and puts the code after them, while the this-binding fix is split across loose lines.
